trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR. This proof is unusually honest about its own gaps (it names an unstated bridge, cites the audit doc, and separates the structural from the canonical gap), and the .ts uses[] comment even explains why conj:brane-tower-z-habiro is deliberately NOT listed. Two defects survive that. (1) THE TELESCOPE NEEDS alpha_k = 1 AND SAYS SO NOWHERE. Step 3 introduces m = Sum_{k=0}^{k_star} alpha_k * m^{(k)}; Step 4 sets m^{(k)}|_i = Phi^{[<=k]}(z_i) - Phi^{[<=k-1]}(z_i) and then asserts Sum_k alpha_k * m^{(k)}|_i = Phi^{[<=k_star]}(z_i). A telescoping sum of consecutive differences collapses to the top term only when every coefficient is 1 (and with the convention Phi^{[<=-1]} = 0, which is also unstated; note Phi^{[<=0]} is the empty product 1, so the k = 0 term is 1). With general alpha_k the sum is Sum_k (alpha_k - alpha_{k+1}) Phi^{[<=k]} + alpha_{k_star} Phi^{[<=k_star]}, which is not the claimed value. Either define alpha_k = 1 and remove them, or carry them through Step 4. (2) MINOR, typography: the display closing Step 4's telescope ends with a comma and is followed by a new sentence beginning 'The brane-tower contribution ...' with a capital letter — the comma should be a full stop. VERIFIED OK: Phi_q^{[<=k]}(z) = prod_{j=1}^{k} (1 - q^{-j} z)^{-1} does have exactly k factors as claimed ('a finite product of k_star(T_w) factors'), and with q_0 > 1 the q^{-j} convention is the convergent one.
